info.text:
Paying off your last open loan early can lower your FICO score. Usually briefly.
myFICO says a loan with a low balance looks less risky than having no open installment loan at all, so paying off your last one can cost points.
Experian and Equifax also point to credit mix (10% of a FICO score) and say the dip is usually small and temporary. Payment history, the biggest factor at 35%, isn't erased by payoff.
A closed loan paid on time can stay on your Experian report for up to 10 years.
Our math: a $10,000 car loan at 7% for 5 years costs $1,881 in interest; paying off the $6,413 left after 2 years skips $716 (assuming no prepayment fee).
FICO-specific; VantageScore and other models may differ.
Sources: myFICO, Experian, Equifax; amortization is our math.
News and education, not financial advice.
